prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: It shall promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations, racial or religious groups,
DEMAND: It shall promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations, racial or religious groups
BEARER: education

cli.result:
1. Education must promote each of understanding, tolerance and friendship, and each one must be promoted among all nations, all racial groups and all religious groups.
2. Education must promote understanding, tolerance and friendship as one combined aim among all of these groups. It meets the demand by promoting the three together, not by promoting each one separately.
3. Education must promote understanding, tolerance and friendship within each category taken separately: among all nations, among all racial groups, and among all religious groups. It is not required to promote them between groups of different kinds.
4. Education must promote understanding, tolerance and friendship across the whole set of nations, racial groups and religious groups taken together. This includes relations between groups of different kinds, such as between a nation and a religious group.
5. Education must promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations, and also among either racial groups or religious groups, whichever it chooses. This reads "or" as a real choice; it is a less natural reading.
